A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PAB benchmark and CMP framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–B are readable and support comparison, including material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original PAB retrieval experiments, component and training-data ablations, qualitative retrieval results, and an appendix comparison with RaSa.

after.justification: v2 reports original PAB experiments, expanded method comparisons, ablations, and out-of-distribution retrieval results on the newly constructed UCC test set.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 and Figure 3 revise the pose pathway: v1 feeds the pose map directly into the image encoder, whereas v2 inserts a Pose Conv module containing convolution, batch normalization, and ReLU. The broader encoder framework, IHNM procedure, and three training objectives remain.

E1.justification: v2 adds UCC, an out-of-distribution test set of 5,320 image-text pairs extracted from UCF-Crime videos covering 13 types. This substantially extends evaluation beyond the OOPS-derived PAB test set. The original PAB training and test collections retain their reported sizes.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates an APTM-derived baseline and includes RaSa in Appendix B.3. v2 Table 2 expands the evaluated methods to APTM, RaSa, IRRA, CLIP, and X-VLM, with zero-shot and fine-tuned comparisons. X-VLM also replaces the APTM-derived model as the principal baseline.

E3.justification: CMP initialization changes from APTM to X-VLM, and component ablations change from 100,000 to 1M training pairs while retaining 30 epochs. v2 adds an external-test protocol using PAB-trained models on UCC. Its training-data sweep also omits the previously reported 50% point. These are substantive reported setting changes.

E4.justification: v2 adds an explicit distribution-shift evaluation on UCC and extends training-data sensitivity analysis to both PAB and UCC. The PE and IHNM ablation questions are retained under revised settings. The scale plot changes from PAB R@1/R@5/R@10 to R@1 on two datasets.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, variability estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The revised tables and plots continue to present point estimates without uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Most retrieval results are replaced or expanded. Full-data CMP changes from 79.53% R@1 and 88.17% mAP in v1 to 84.93% and 91.66% in v2; v2 additionally reports 55.23% R@1 and 44.35% mAP on UCC. Main-text and appendix retrieval rankings also change. These are revised results under changed model settings, not a controlled version-to-version gain.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 retain the same attention, matching, contrastive, MLM, and combined-loss formulations. v2 clarifies notation, including the attention dimension d, but introduces no substantive mathematical derivation, formal assumption, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The central task, benchmark, and pose-aware retrieval contributions remain. The empirical contribution is broadened from improvement over the original PAB baseline to explicitly claimed competitiveness on both PAB and unseen UCC. The abstract replaces the 2.88-point improvement claim with 84.93% R@1 and a claim of surpassing competitive methods.

C2.justification: v2 interprets UCC results as evidence of adaptability to unseen datasets, connects this evaluation to open-set characteristics, and argues that PAB's elevated anomaly ratio supports robust learning. It also links competitive performance with limited training data to hard-negative sampling. Existing caption-noise and privacy qualifications remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents Pose Conv composition and UCC construction, and replaces the promised resource release with an availability statement and repository address. Actual availability cannot be verified from the PDFs. Appendix training and reranking details are retained, while the original dataset-resolution and split-specific caption-length table details are omitted.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against video anomaly detection through the introduction, redesigned Table 1, and new Appendix A.3/Table 6. It discusses annotation granularity, anomaly imbalance, and synthetic-to-real differences. Added references include UCA, video anomaly retrieval, PLOT, and X-VLM; the earlier NWPU discussion is removed.

P1.justification: The introduction and contribution statements are extensively rewritten, and the conclusion is condensed and revised. Section 5 replaces its previous subsection organization with topical paragraphs, incorporating the expanded comparisons. Appendix sections are reorganized, alongside numerous terminology, wording, and cross-reference corrections.

P2.justification: Table 1 is redesigned, the original split-statistics table disappears, and Figure 3 is redrawn. The combined results/ablation figure is replaced by separate tables and a two-dataset line plot. New comparison tables appear in the main text and appendix, while qualitative figures are updated and relocated.

improvement.justification: v1's validation is confined to PAB with narrow method comparisons. v2's broader zero-shot and fine-tuned comparisons and external UCC evaluation substantially strengthen the evidence for benchmark usefulness and model generalization. Changed initialization prevents attributing higher scores solely to CMP, and uncertainty reporting remains absent, but the expanded validation addresses an important weakness of the earlier paper.
